enriched.title: Estruturas Gramaticais e Vocabulário do Cotidiano em Inglês
enriched.summary: A aula aborda estruturas gramaticais úteis no dia a dia, como expressões envolvendo causative verbs e o uso correto de tempos verbais. Também inclui vocabulário prático relacionado a hábitos, transporte, reciclagem e atividades físicas, além de dicas de pronúncia.
mainTopics: Uso de tempos verbais no cotidiano (Present Simple, Past Continuous)
Vocabulário sobre transporte, reciclagem e atividades físicas
Diferenciação de palavras e expressões comuns

vocabulary.definition: To teach a particular skill or type of behavior through practice and instruction; a series of connected railway cars.
examples: I like to train at the gym every morning.
They took a train to the city center.

vocabulary.definition: To organize or arrange things that are not in order or are untidy.
examples: We need to sort out the garbage before taking it out.
She sorted out the books by genre.
Sort out the garbage into recyclable and non-recyclable materials.
The garbage truck comes every morning.

vocabulary.definition: A rectangular area marked with lines for playing tennis.
examples: Do you and your friend play tennis together on the tennis court?
The tennis court is booked for a match this evening.

vocabulary.definition: Physical activity that you do to make your body strong and healthy.
examples: My mother goes to the gym every day to do exercise.
He does exercise in the morning to start his day right.

grammar.explanation: Causative verbs are used to indicate that someone causes another person to do something or that something is done for them.
rules: 'Have + object + past participle': Used when someone arranges for another person to do something.
'Get + object + past participle': Often used in informal situations with the same meaning as 'have'.
commonMistakes: Using 'make' instead of 'have' or 'get' in causative constructions.
Forgetting to use the past participle after 'have' or 'get'.

grammar.explanation: The Present Simple is used for habits and general truths, while the Past Continuous is used for ongoing actions in the past.
rules: Use Present Simple for routines or repeated actions.
Use Past Continuous to describe actions that were in progress at a specific time in the past.
examples: Lorna often watches series in the evening, but Alice is usually on Instagram.
At this time last year, we were planning that big project.
commonMistakes: Using Present Simple to talk about an action that was happening in the past.
Forgetting to use 'was/were' + verb in -ing form for Past Continuous.

expressions.usage: Usado para se referir ao planejamento de algo com antecedência.
examples: Let’s make arrangements for another day.

expressions.usage: Usado para falar de organizar ou separar o lixo corretamente.
examples: Sort out the garbage before recycling.

expressions.usage: Usado para descrever mudanças no tempo ou no ambiente.
examples: It’s getting very cold. Let’s go inside.

practiceQuestions.question: Write a sentence using 'have + past participle' to describe something you arranged to be done.
practiceQuestions.answer: I had my car cleaned yesterday.
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'Have + past participle' is used to describe when someone arranges for an action to be done by someone else.

practiceQuestions.question: Translate to English: Minha mãe vai à academia todos os dias, mas meu pai não faz nenhum exercício.
practiceQuestions.answer: My mother goes to the gym every day, but my father doesn’t do any exercise.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Use Present Simple for habitual actions and negate with 'doesn't' for third person singular.

practiceQuestions.question: Identify the error: 'I have my house paint by a professional painter.'
practiceQuestions.answer: The correct sentence is: 'I had my house painted by a professional painter.'
practiceQuestions.explanation: In causative verbs, the past participle form of the verb should be used.

culturalNotes: Separar o lixo (recycling) é uma prática comum em muitos países de língua inglesa, especialmente em locais como Canadá e países da Europa. É importante conhecer o vocabulário relacionado para se adaptar a essas culturas.
O uso de transporte público é amplamente incentivado em várias cidades do mundo anglófono, como Londres e Nova York, onde o transporte público é uma parte essencial da vida cotidiana.
studyTips: Pratique a diferença entre 'do' e 'make' com exemplos do cotidiano para evitar confusões comuns.
Use aplicativos de pronúncia para ouvir e repetir palavras como 'train' e 'garbage' para melhorar sua fluência.
originalExamples: I had my hair cut. (Eu cortei meu cabelo.)
You had your house painted. (Você pintou sua casa.)
Let’s meet up another day. (Vamos nos encontrar outro dia.)
Let’s make arrangements for another day. (Vamos fazer arranjos para outro dia.)
Lorna often watches series in the evening, but Alice is usually on Instagram. (Lorna frequentemente assiste séries à noite, mas Alice geralmente fica no Instagram.)
I am often tired. I work hard and I don’t relax much. (Eu estou frequentemente cansado. Eu trabalho duro e não relaxo muito.)
My mother goes to the gym every day, but my father doesn’t do any exercise. (Minha mãe vai à academia todos os dias, mas meu pai não faz nenhum exercício.)
Do you often use public transportation? (Você usa transporte público com frequência?)
Does your family recycle paper, plastic and glass? (Sua família recicla papel, plástico e vidro?)
Do you and your friend play tennis together? (Você e seu amigo jogam tênis juntos?)
Who is giving the training this week? (Quem está dando o treinamento esta semana?)
It rains a lot here. (Chove muito aqui.)
Who is making this horrible noise? (Quem está fazendo esse barulho horrível?)
Is she making this horrible noise? (Ela está fazendo esse barulho horrível?)
It’s getting very cold. Let’s go inside. (Está ficando muito frio. Vamos para dentro.)
Please put the book into/inside the box. (Por favor, coloque o livro dentro da caixa.)
At this time last year, we were planning that big project. (Nessa época no ano passado, nós estávamos planejando aquele grande projeto.)
It was chaos at the airport last night. Thousands of people were waiting for their flights. (Estava um caos no aeroporto ontem à noite. Milhares de pessoas estavam esperando por seus voos.)
Where was grandma going when you saw her this morning? (Para onde a vó estava indo quando você a viu esta manhã?)
I’m going to return the help that I received creating a soup kitchen for children. (Eu vou retribuir a ajuda que recebi criando um sopão para crianças.)
